config_name: XPS 13 — Core Ultra 7 355, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 13.4" 2.5K touch 120Hz (Storm)

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 7 355 (Series 3 Panther Lake, 8-core, up to 4.7 GHz)

battery.notes: Same 70Wh-class platform as mid tier; ~10-13h light use estimated.

reviews.quote: It's great to see Dell bring back the XPS and do so with such style.

praises: 32GB in a 1 kg chassis is nearly unique — this is the road-warrior config that actually survives 2026 Chrome-tab loads
$800 off est. value at Black Friday softens Dell's usual config tax
120Hz 2.5K touch panel stays smooth and bright (500 nits) outdoors
Copilot+ NPU handles local AI features without a dGPU
Owners repeatedly praise fast boot times and quiet, efficient cooling (dell.ca review summary)
complaints: Even at $2,300 you get the same 2-speaker, 2-port package — the money buys RAM, not features
Soldered everything; at this price buyers expect at least a replaceable SSD
Some owners report keyboard feel problems and occasional hardware faults (dell.ca review summary)
Steep $650 premium over the 16GB/512GB tier for modest real-world gains

design_philosophy: The max-memory XPS 13 tier proves the chassis concept: Dell's thinnest, lightest premium laptop configured for people who refuse to carry weight but refuse 16GB. It trades any thermal headroom for RAM density.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 14 (2026) 8.1 anchor + dell.ca specs. +0.5 productivity vs 16GB tier for 32GB headroom (per SCHEMA 'more RAM → productivity +0.5').
